instructions:
Access to Kleros arbitration data: courts, disputes, evidence, jurors and PNK stakes.

Pass one of these as the `chain` argument:

  arbitrum-one              Kleros v2 Beta. The LIVE production deployment - real disputes, real
                            arbitration fees, real money. "Beta" is the release, not a test network.
  arbitrum-sepolia-testnet  Kleros v2 Testnet. Test data only.
  ethereum                  Kleros v1. Live production.
  gnosis                    Kleros v1. Live production.

When someone asks about real, current or production disputes without naming a chain, they mean
arbitrum-one. Never answer a question about live activity with Testnet data.

`arbitrum-sepolia` is RETIRED and is now refused. It named the Devnet -
`arbitrum-sepolia-devnet` - which is a DIFFERENT deployment from the Testnet above, so migrating
it to the Testnet slug silently changes which disputes you read.

DEGRADED IS NORMAL, and commonest on the Testnet: dispute_get and dispute_brief come back partial
with `unresolvedFields` set, and dispute_policy errors outright. Report it as that dispute's
state, not a service fault.

WHAT YOU GET IF YOU OMIT chain. Most tools fan out over ethereum, gnosis and arbitrum-one, in
that order, and nothing else - the Testnet and the Devnet are reached only by name. List tools
drain them sequentially: page one is entirely ethereum, later chains follow only once the
earlier ones are drained. An absent result on page one means "not on
ethereum yet", not "does not exist". Echo nextCursor back verbatim; a cursor ending in a colon
with nothing after it marks a chain boundary, not the end of the data.

CHAIN IS MANDATORY FOR SEVEN TOOLS - arbitrable_classify, juror_info, dispute_brief,
dispute_policy, and court_get, court_policy and juror_top when given a court. Without one they
fail rather than fan out; calling again unchanged will not succeed.

FAILURES CARRY NO ERROR CODE FIELD - only isError and prose. Branch on isError, then read the
text: names like IPFS_UNAVAILABLE below appear in it, never as a field to switch on.

RESULTS MAY SUGGEST NEXT STEPS AS COMMAND LINES, successes included. You cannot run those - read
the tool and arguments out of them and call the tool.

RULING STATE. `ruled` does not mean the same thing on both Kleros generations: on v1 it turns
true once the ruling was executed against the arbitrable contract, on v2 once the dispute
reached its execution period, which may lag notification. Every row carries a `ruledSemantics`
marker reading `executed`, `period-reached` or `onchain`. Branch on that marker, never on
the chain name.

When the ruling must be current use dispute_get, not dispute_list: dispute_get reads the
arbitrator contract live, dispute_list is a subgraph snapshot and can show a dispute ruled
before the arbitrable was notified.

POLICIES COME IN PAIRS. Never answer from dispute_policy alone. On ethereum and gnosis (Kleros
v1) the constraint binding a juror is the INTERSECTION of court_policy and dispute_policy, so
reading one of them misses the half that narrows it. On the Kleros v2 deployments there is no
intersection rule: the two documents come from independent sources and neither narrows the
other. Read both everywhere; intersect only on v1.

IPFS_UNAVAILABLE means the content needs repinning, not that you picked the wrong gateway.
Report it unavailable and suggest retrying later. Do not propose another gateway - the one in
use already fans out server-side, so a swap hides the signal without fixing it.

Evidence items with binary attachments carry an `extractionHint`. Hand that to a
document-extraction tool rather than reporting the attachment unreadable.

Two silent traps in arbitrable_classify. Its `category` is advisory free text pulled from
unstructured metadata - show it, never branch on it. And on the Kleros v2 deployments a
miss returns type `unknown` because only the curated registry is consulted there; read that as
"not in the registry", never as "confirmed not a Kleros contract".

CREATING A DISPUTE. dispute_create files against your organisation's dispute template.
The court, juror count and template are fixed for you, and this call sends them:
court 8, 5 jurors, on arbitrum-sepolia-testnet.
This spends real arbitration fees from your organisation's wallet.
Name parties with the REQUIRED `aliases` argument, keyed by slot: client, provider.
Pass only the ones you know, and `{}` when you know none: an empty argument object is refused,
never filed. An omitted slot is left out of the filed template - do NOT pass a zero address
or a placeholder, it is refused.

PUBLISHING AN ATTACHMENT. evidence_pin takes a file as base64 plus its extension and returns
the `/ipfs/<cid>` URI an Evidence document references. It fetches no URL.
Publication is PERMANENT and PUBLIC - never call it to experiment. You get `status:
"published"` and the URI once the CID is confirmed to address your bytes. Retrying after a
failure is safe and spends nothing.

SUBMITTING AN EVIDENCE DOCUMENT. evidence_submit records a `name`, a `description` and
optionally one `fileUri` against a dispute, so the jurors deciding it read your account.
`dispute` is the Core dispute ID - the number Kleros Court shows. `evidence_list` does NOT take
it: it keys on the arbitrable's own ID, which a mined dispute_create returns beside it as
`localDisputeID` - when absent, the payload says why. Keep both. Confirm the Core ID first -
another real dispute's ID is accepted, indexed and wrong. Put your account in `description` as
prose - a bare URI there becomes the whole document and the jurors read nothing. An
Attachment goes in `fileUri`, recorded as given and never fetched.
This spends gas from your organisation's wallet and the document is PUBLIC and PERMANENT.
If a call fails once the transaction was sent, do NOT submit again: an empty `evidence_list` is
not proof. Report the txHash for a human to resolve. A duplicate costs gas and shows
the jurors the same document twice; it creates no second dispute.

ONE WRITE AT A TIME per organisation. A write sent while another runs is refused
WRITE_IN_PROGRESS: nothing was sent, so call again once that one returns.
